issue.title: Flake gate counts audit failures from dirty workspaces, so one agent's in-progress edit blocks everyone's check-full
issue.description:
DISCOVERED while running 'just check-full' for an unrelated TUI change in workspace sase_19 at commit 31b9c62b6805 (2026-08-13T20:03Z). The run's own full pytest lane passed clean (29682 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failures), and only 'just selection-health --fail-on-new-flake' failed.

ROOT CAUSE (proved from the durable store, not inferred): reproducible-flake classification consumes full-run records that were recorded from DIRTY workspace trees, so a source-tree audit that an agent's own uncommitted edits legitimately broke is promoted into shared cross-workspace flake debt and then blocks 'just check-full' for every other agent.

EVIDENCE. tests/test_agent_artifact_marker_path_passing_audit.py::test_tracked_marker_path_passing_sites_are_reviewed was flagged as a reproducible flake on exactly two records in ~/.sase/test-selection/gh_sase-org__sase, and BOTH carry changed_files that overlap the very tree the audit walks:
  - 20260812T230235Z-9f93c3d8c0c5-2782438-full-run.json (workspace sase_12, exit 1, 2 failures) changed_files: src/sase/monitor/, src/sase/plan_chain.py, tests/monitor/, tests/test_plan_chain_roles.py
  - 20260813T194513Z-1004f9eb33d6-2320907-full-run.json (workspace sase_16, exit 1, 2 failures) changed_files: src/sase/monitor/supervise.py, src/sase/monitor/settlement.py, src/sase/monitor/start.py, src/sase/monitor/reconcile.py, src/sase/ace/tui/models/_loaders/_workflow_loaders.py, and 7 more

The audit asserts _path_passing_contexts() == set(_REVIEWED_PATH_PASSING_CONTEXTS) (tests/test_agent_artifact_marker_path_passing_audit.py:111), i.e. an AST scan of src/sase compared against a checked-in reviewed inventory whose entries include 'src/sase/monitor/supervise.py:_read_meta' and the monitor start entries. Editing those files without updating the inventory breaks the audit DETERMINISTICALLY in that workspace. That is correct, intended behavior for the editing agent -- it is not a flake, and it is not a break on master. On a clean tree here the file passes in isolation (2 passed in 13.25s).

The sibling node tests/test_agent_artifact_marker_mutation_audit.py::test_tracked_marker_mutation_sites_are_reviewed failed in the same sase_16 record, confirming the class generalizes to every marker-audit node and, more broadly, to any source-tree audit test.

WHY THIS IS NOT sase-hl: sase-hl (closed done 2026-08-08) covered a DIFFERENT false-positive mode -- a node deterministically broken on master that different workspaces report alongside disjoint diffs -- and proposed distinguishing it by checking whether the node fails consistently across ALL full runs after some commit. That remedy does not help here: these are two isolated failures among many passing full runs, so the dirty-tree case still reads as genuine intermittency under sase-hl's proposed rule. Different root cause, different remediation.

IMPACT: the gate is currently blocking 'just check-full' for every landing agent that hits this node, and the 30-day record retention means a single mid-edit run keeps poisoning the shared gate for weeks after the editing agent has landed or abandoned the change.

SCOPE: decide and implement the correct attribution rule in tests/_test_selection_health.py / tools/selection_health -- for example, do not feed a full-run record's failures into reproducible-flake determination when the record's changed_files overlap the sources a failing audit scans, or record tree-dirtiness on the run record and discount dirty-tree records the way max_failures_per_run already discounts catastrophic runs. Add a regression that reconstructs the two records above and asserts the node is not classified as a reproducible flake.
